title: Medicare Supplement Plan Considerations
source: Dugan K et al. JAMA Network Open. 2025;8(4):e252834 — eAppendix 4
question_text: What is a Medicare Supplement Plan, how much do they cost, and when do I enroll?

accurate_complete: Supplement plans can be purchased separately if you choose traditional Medicare, to help cover out-of-pocket costs
All supplement plans cover Part A and Part B copays and hospital and hospice costs
Some supplement plans cover Part A and Part B deductibles
Some supplement plans have out-of-pocket limits
Supplement plan costs vary based on how much is covered, but usually range from $50–$300 per month
You can enroll in a Supplement plan at any time
You will get better rates if you enroll during your open enrollment period (which begins the day you turn 65 and lasts for six months afterwards)
accurate_incomplete: Some (but not all) of the Medicare Supplement Plan topics were substantively discussed
not_substantive: None of the Medicare Supplement Plan topics were substantively discussed
Counselor said they do not know
Otherwise did not substantively answer the question
incorrect: Incorrect information was provided that was substantive enough to materially change the substance of the answer or affect an enrollee's coverage decision

scoring_notes: All 7 criteria must be covered for Accurate and Complete. The 3.1% baseline reflects how comprehensive the rubric is. The most commonly missed facts are the open enrollment timing / rate guarantee and the cost range. 'Medigap' is an acceptable synonym for Medicare Supplement Plan.
